title: UV sensitive vision in cardinals and tanagers is ubiquitous
why: Chlorophanes spiza, lambda_max_nm and spectral_range_nm: partial SWS1 opsin sequences from a broad sample of Cardinalidae and Thraupidae (all of the UV-sensitive type, per the abstract that earlier sweeps read), so its species table, unseen, may hold the green honeycreeper and give its SWS1 class; a gene survey predicts a pigment class and measures no peak, so it bears on the Ultraviolet row at the lowest grade. Main holds the UV-sensitive type of Cyanerpes cyaneus, another honeycreeper genus (Odeen and Hastad 2013 and the 2011 passerine survey), and no Chlorophanes row. Neither this unit's harvest nor its spectral searches returned it; the citation is the one on main's wanted lists (harvest-37 line 6, with the Crossref year 2020, and sweep-10, -16, -23, -25, -41 and -51 for other tanager genera), and authors are left to the registry.

title: Morphological traits of the eyes of Lepidoptera indicate selection for binocular vision in both diurnal butterflies and nocturnal moths
why: Chioides, acuity_cpd and interommatidial_deg: an eye-model study of 2,730 specimens of 224 butterfly and moth species sampled across a tribal-level phylogeny of butterflies, so its species table may include the white-striped longtail or another Chioides with eye measurements bearing on resolution. The Hesperiidae vision review returned it for this genus, and the stored abstract names no species. Main's wanted lists hold it for other skipper genera (harvest-30, -33 and -34), and the desk holds the Lepidoptera acuity records of earlier units on the same work. Not opened; authors are left to the registry.
